title: Shared definitions
description: Reusable primitive definitions shared by every fsu-schedule schema. This file declares no root type of its own; it exists only to be referenced via $ref (for example, "common.defs.schema.json#/$defs/timeOfDay"). TIME POLICY for the entire fsu-schedule data model: all clock times are wall-clock "HH:MM" strings in 24-hour form, and all dates are ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DD" strings. Both are interpreted in the America/New_York timezone, which is the single timezone of every FSU campus. Naive local datetimes (a date and time fused into one string with no zone) are never used anywhere in this model: a point in absolute time is always an RFC 3339 timestamp carrying an explicit UTC offset. This split is deliberate. A class that meets at 09:05 meets at 09:05 on both sides of a daylight-saving transition, so its time must stay a wall-clock string bound to a named zone rather than a fixed instant; whereas an event that actually happened, such as a schedule import, is a real instant and must carry its offset.

date.description: A calendar date in ISO-8601 extended form, YYYY-MM-DD, interpreted in America/New_York. Example: "2026-08-24".

timestamp.description: An absolute point in time as an RFC 3339 timestamp. The trailing UTC offset (or literal Z) is REQUIRED by the pattern so that naive local datetimes fail validation. Example: "2026-08-27T14:03:11-04:00".

timeOfDay.description: A wall-clock time of day, 24-hour "HH:MM", zero-padded, in America/New_York. Range 00:00 through 23:59. Example: "09:05". Use timeOfDayInclusiveEnd instead when the value is the exclusive end of a window that may run to midnight.

timeOfDayInclusiveEnd.description: A wall-clock time in America/New_York used as the EXCLUSIVE end of a time window, 24-hour "HH:MM". Accepts the extra value "24:00" to mean end-of-day, which lets a window run to midnight without wrapping. A window whose end is less than or equal to its start is invalid; express an overnight span as two windows instead.

dayOfWeek.description: A day of the week, spelled out in lowercase English. FSU's own registration systems abbreviate days as M/T/W/R/F/S/U (note that R means Thursday and U means Sunday); importers MUST normalize those single letters to these long forms rather than storing the abbreviations.

dayOfWeekList.description: A set of weekdays. Order is not significant, but writers SHOULD emit Monday-first order for readability. Values must be unique.

timeWindow.description: A recurring weekly window of wall-clock time: a set of weekdays plus a start and an exclusive end, all in America/New_York. Used for parking enforcement rules and for pedestrian crowd factors. The window does not wrap past midnight; split overnight spans into two windows.

daysOfWeek.description: The weekdays this window applies to.

endTime.description: Exclusive end of the window. Must be strictly later than startTime; use "24:00" for end-of-day.

latitude.description: WGS-84 latitude in decimal degrees. Deliberately clamped to Florida's bounding box (24 to 32) rather than the full -90 to 90 range, so that a swapped or sign-flipped coordinate pair fails validation loudly instead of silently placing a building in the ocean.

longitude.description: WGS-84 longitude in decimal degrees. Deliberately clamped to Florida's bounding box (-88 to -79) rather than the full -180 to 180 range, so that a swapped or sign-flipped coordinate pair fails validation loudly. FSU's Tallahassee campuses sit near -84.3; the Panama City campus near -85.6.

buildingCode.description: An FSU building code in uppercase, as printed on a class schedule: 2 to 8 characters, starting with a letter. Examples: "HCB", "HWC", "WMS". This is the primary key that joins course meetings, walk-graph nodes, and parking zones to buildings.

termCode.description: A stable identifier for an academic term, formed as the calendar year of the term followed by its season: "YYYY-season". Examples: "2026-fall", "2027-spring". The year is the year the term's classes begin, so FSU's spring term that runs January through April 2027 is "2027-spring". Sub-sessions within a summer term are modelled as sessions inside term-calendar rather than as separate term codes.

slug.description: A stable lowercase kebab-case identifier. Used for entrance ids, walk-graph node and edge ids, parking rule ids, and calendar entry ids. Must remain stable across data releases, because other records reference it.

confidence.description: How much a value should be trusted. "verified" means checked against an authoritative FSU source or measured in person; "estimated" means derived, interpolated, or eyeballed; "unknown" means carried over without review. Answers given to students SHOULD hedge when the supporting data is not verified.

sourceAttribution.description: Where a piece of shipped static data came from and when it was last checked, so stale campus data can be found and refreshed.

url.description: The authoritative page or document this data was taken from.

label.description: Human-readable name of the source, for example "FSU Transportation and Parking Services permit map".

retrievedAt.description: When the source was last fetched.
